title: GPR Signature Classification for Common Pipe Materials in Vojvodina Soils: A Laboratory and Field Study

record.title: GPR Signature Classification for Common Pipe Materials in Vojvodina Soils: A Laboratory and Field Study
record.abstract: Distinguishing pipe material from GPR reflections alone is commercially useful because material type determines corrosion risk and replacement priority. This laboratory and field study characterised GPR reflections from steel, cast iron, ductile iron, PVC and high-density polyethylene pipes of 63–315 mm diameter buried in reconstructed Vojvodina soil columns at 0.5–2.0 m depth. Four antenna frequencies (250, 500, 900 and 1600 MHz) were evaluated. Amplitude-versus-offset behaviour, reflection polarity and hyperbola apex sharpness were extracted as discriminating features and fed into a random forest classifier. In controlled conditions the classifier separated metallic from non-metallic pipes with 96% accuracy; distinguishing PVC from HDPE remained unreliable at all frequencies tested. Field trials over 12.1 km of surveyed distribution network in Ruma and Inđija showed that metallic versus non-metallic classification transferred to field conditions with 89% accuracy when soil moisture was below 20% volumetric content, degrading to 74% under wet conditions.
